title: Let an agent run a website and its ad budget
summary: A developer gave Claude Code a website, ad accounts and a budget to manage every four hours; he says it mostly churns out search-bait pages and share buttons.
agent_role: Claude Code edits the site and manages ad campaigns on a recurring four-hour schedule; the human set up access and budget and watches.
outcome: Author reports the agent mostly does 'tomfoolery' such as creating many SEO pages and adding share buttons to try to go viral.
what_they_did: A developer who builds websites gave Claude Code a starter site and a budget. It got access to ad accounts on Google, X, LinkedIn and Reddit, plus tools for gathering web data and using other AI models. The site tailors content to each visitor based on their device, location and behavior. Claude Code reviews the site and takes action every four hours.
how_it_went: The author says it mostly does tomfoolery so far. It makes lots of pages aimed at search engines and adds share buttons to try to go viral, much like interns suggest. He still enjoys watching its choices.
worth_knowing: The site reads about fifty signals from each visitor's device and can look up public profiles, so it asks for consent first and offers to erase data. Giving an agent a live ad budget puts real money at risk.
prompt: Every 4 hours, review [your website repo] and its analytics, then propose up to three changes to the site or to my ad campaigns on [ad platforms] within a total budget of [budget]. Explain the reasoning for each change. Show me the plan and any ad spend changes and wait for my approval before deploying site changes or changing campaigns.

curation.rationale: A real autonomous experiment where Claude Code runs a website and ad accounts on a 4-hour loop, but results are thin and anecdotal. The heavy visitor-profiling design adds privacy concerns, though the site discloses it and asks consent.
